items.q: Are the 2 trial sessions really free?
items.a: Yes — completely free, no card and no commitment.
If you’d like to continue, you choose a monthly plan. If not, there’s nothing to cancel.

items.q: Can I request a specific teacher?
items.a: Yes — mention their name when you book and we’ll do our best to match you.

items.q: What if I don’t speak Arabic?
items.a: Every teacher is fully bilingual in Arabic and English, and many students start from zero.
The Itqan method: mastery and reflection (Tadabbur), not just recitation — thematic verse grouping and real-time correction instead of rote repetition.

items.q: Do I get a certificate or Ijazah?
items.a: Every student receives a certificate per level. Recitation and Hifz students can work toward a formal Ijazah with a documented chain back to the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Azhar University graduates holding Ijazahs, experienced with both Arabic and non-Arabic speakers.

items.q: Can I request a female teacher for my daughter or wife?
items.a: Yes — dedicated female teachers for women and children, in a private, faith-conscious setting.
Zoom or Google Meet, with an interactive whiteboard for marking up Tajweed.

items.q: What if I miss a session?
items.a: Reschedule free with 24 hours’ notice, so a missed session isn’t a lost one.

items.q: Do you cover my time zone?
items.a: Yes — lessons run around the clock, so you book the time that genuinely suits you.

items.q: My child is 5 — is that too young?
items.a: Not at all — Ummah Cubs welcomes children from age 5 with short, game-based 30-minute lessons.

items.q: Can I track my child’s progress?
items.a: A report after every lesson and monthly badges, with one Family Portal account for all your children; the live dashboard and recording library are rolling out.
